result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cycle_basis()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a fundamental cycle basis of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L9711-L9798){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cycle_basis(root=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A cycle basis is a minimal set of cycles such that any cycle in the graph can be expressed as a symmetric difference (XOR) of cycles in the basis. For a connected graph with `V` vertices and `E` edges, the cycle basis has exactly `E - V + 1` cycles (the cyclomatic complexity). The algorithm builds a spanning tree using BFS from a root node, then for each non-tree edge (back edge), finds the fundamental cycle it creates with the tree. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [root]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional root node ID to start BFS from. If `None`, uses an arbitrary node. Different root nodes may produce different (but equally valid) cycle bases. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of cycles forming the cycle basis. Each cycle is a list of node IDs. The cycles are fundamental cycles (each contains exactly one back edge). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on a directed graph (cycle basis only applies to undirected graphs). [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the specified root node does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - Time complexity: `O(V + E)` for building spanning tree and finding cycles. - The cycle basis is not unique, different spanning trees yield different bases. - Works on disconnected graphs (finds cycles in each component). - For weighted graphs needing minimum total weight, use `minimum_cycle_basis()`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find the cycle basis of a simple graph: ::: {#2817a6a1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Square with diagonal graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") .add_edge("D", "A") .add_edge("A", "C") # diagonal ) basis = graph.cycle_basis() # Returns 2 (fundamental cycles from the two triangles formed by the diagonal) len(basis) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Specify a root node: ::: {#4fd1b666 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) node_ids = graph.get_node_ids() basis = graph.cycle_basis(root=node_ids[0]) # Returns 1 (the triangle) len(basis) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: :::
